reasons: The locked target is the preferred position — "No non-solicit on Customer" — and deleting paragraph 12.4 in full achieves exactly that: the solicit, hire and employ duties, the 24-month tail and the "regardless of how the employee applies" sweep-up all disappear.

Deletion is the minimal edit here because the entire paragraph consists of nothing but the one-way Customer covenant the playbook rejects; there is no unrelated commercial term inside it that needs preserving, so no operator, number or short-phrase substitution would suffice to reach the preferred (rather than fallback) level. The official minimality gate's generic 'whole paragraph' objection does not apply on these facts.

Intent is preserved and a contradiction is cured: Section 12.3 records that Customer made no no-hire commitment, and removing 12.4 aligns the operative text with that acknowledgement. No defined term, cross-reference or dangling mechanic is introduced.

The fallback bargain is not satisfied (no mutual covenant, no service-personnel scope, no 12-month involvement-based tail, no general-advertisement or unsolicited-approach carve-outs), but that is irrelevant at the locked preferred level and the fallback is correctly offered only in the non-operative margin comment.
